title: GPU pool utilization slices by job-priority (weekly export)
content:
OVERVIEW:
This is a working export from the infra dashboard (weekly) that slices GPU utilization by job priority buckets (high, medium, low) across clusters and pools. Purpose: spot where high-priority workloads are contending, estimate burn/saturation risk, and propose short-term mitigations for next 2 weeks.

CSV_ROWS:
date,cluster,pool,priority_slice,avg_gpu_util_pct,p95_gpu_util_pct,allocated_gpus,running_jobs,burn_rate_gpus_per_day,projected_days_to_saturation
2025-01-05,cluster-a,pool-training,high,86,98,160,42,8.5,~12
2025-01-05,cluster-a,pool-training,medium,42,65,80,38,3.1,~65
2025-01-05,cluster-a,pool-training,low,12,28,20,14,0.6,>180
2025-01-05,cluster-b,pool-inference,high,71,92,96,26,6.0,~16
2025-01-05,cluster-b,pool-inference,medium,30,50,48,21,1.8,~80
2025-01-05,cluster-c,pool-experimental,high,49,76,40,11,2.4,~40

NOTABLE SIGNALS (quick take):
- cluster-a / pool-training: high-priority slice is consistently >80% avg and hitting p95 ~98%. Allocation = 160 GPUs; burn_rate ~8.5 GPUs/day driven by 4 persistent training jobs spinning up larger batches. Projection suggests saturation in ~12 days if trend continues.
- cluster-b / pool-inference: high-priority has occasional spikes (p95 92%) and steady background at ~70% avg; inference autoscaler config might be under-tuning scale-up thresholds for tail spikes.
- cluster-c / pool-experimental: utilization mixed; several medium-priority jobs are large parameter sweeps that could be shifted to low-priority preemptible capacity.

SMALL ASCII CHART (avg util by cluster high-slice last 7 days):
cluster-a: ██████████ 86%
cluster-b: ████████ 71%
cluster-c: ██████ 49%

ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS (short term):
- Add a temporary +32 GPU burst reserve to cluster-a training pool (team: training-platform) for 14 days to avoid canary failures. Rationale: buys ~3–4 days of breathing room while we throttle/optimize big batch jobs.
- Change inference autoscaler policy for pool-inference: lower the scale-up cooldown from 120s -> 45s and add p95-trigger rule targeting concurrency spikes. Owner: SRE.
- Migrate 2 large medium-priority hyperparam sweep jobs from cluster-c to the experimental preemptible pool (or schedule nightly). Contact: Lina to coordinate with ML teams.
- Start quota for new "preemptible-cold" label in scheduler and tag jobs via submitter flag --preferred-preemptible.

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Burn rate estimates assume current job arrival patterns. If a new model training push lands this week (rumored from product), cluster-a projection will be invalid. See linked JIRA-1234.
- We don't have per-organization tagging on all jobs; projection per-customer risk is incomplete. Need a short audit to map top 10 job owners to orgs.
- Are we confident burst reserve billing/commit terms are approved for short-term bursts? Finance check required.

NEXT STEPS / TODO (owner tags inline):
- [Priya] raise short-term burst request for cluster-a via internal finance playbook (due 2025-01-15)
- [SRE / Marco] update autoscaler policy PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/678) and run canary (due 2025-01-16)
- [Lina] contact research leads to reschedule sweeps (due 2025-01-14)
- [Infra] one-day audit of job tagging to report top-10 owners and map to priority slices (due 2025-01-17)

APPENDIX (method notes):
- Metrics pulled from internal metrics pipeline (prometheus -> bigquery export) with a 5m sampling window. High/medium/low priority defined by submitter labels + automated bump rules in scheduler (see infra-policy doc).
- burn_rate_gpus_per_day computed as net change in used allocation over 7d smoothed window; projection_days_to_saturation computed as (allocated_gpus * (1 - avg_util_pct/100)) / burn_rate, clipped when burn_rate < 0.5 to >180.

RAW_QUERIES / LINKS:
- BigQuery: projects/infra/datasets/gpu_metrics.tables/weekly_slices?start=2025-01-05
- Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-inference.internal/gpu/slices/weekly?view=priority
- Slack thread: #infra (T0ABCD123)

NOTES_TO_SELF:
- This is a working export; numbers will be re-run after autoscaler PR merges. Keep this doc in drive for 2 weeks then archive.
summary: Working weekly export that slices GPU utilization by priority bucket across clusters; highlights cluster-a training pool at risk and lists short-term mitigations and owners.
